articles.title: Trevor Lawrence: Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback finally hitting lofty heights expected from former No 1 overall pick
articles.summary: Trevor Lawrence was the No 1 overall NFL Draft pick in 2021 and has helped the Jacksonville Jaguars become Super Bowl contenders after a rocky start to his career; watch Jaguars vs Texans at Wembley live on Sky Sports from 2pm on Sunday
articles.body:
The Jags were coming off a 1-15 season and an astonishing 11 losing campaigns out of the previous 13. They are one of just four teams in the NFL to have never played in a Super Bowl.

Conversely, Lawrence arrived having won 34 of his 36 games in college and 52 of 54 in high school. He was supposed to bring those wins to Florida.

Safe to say, that did not happen. As a rookie, he was thrown right in and lost more games in five weeks than he had in five years.

The Urban Meyer head coaching experiment was a disaster and Jacksonville managed just three wins that year.

Lawrence and the Jags' campaigns in the subsequent three years under Meyer's replacement Doug Pederson were a mixed bag that included a playoff win, but ultimately a 4-13 season saw Pederson fired.

Enter Liam Coen, long-time NFL quarterback coach and offensive coordinator who was poached from Tampa Bay in January 2025. Coen's arrival, and Lawrence's development during his tenure, have put the 27-year-old in the mix for NFL MVP and the Jags up there as Super Bowl contenders.

Since the start of last season, the Jaguars have won 17 games out of 22, tied for the best regular-season record in the league. Despite a heart-breaking final-minute defeat to Buffalo in the postseason, year one for Coen ended with the second-best record for the Jags in franchise history (13-4).

Lawrence's ascension was a large part of that but he may be getting even better - and the 4-1 Jags have started hot.

Last year, he offered the volume but not the efficiency. He finished sixth in passing yards (4,007) and fifth in touchdowns (29), but only 28th in completion percentage (60.9), 20th in quarterback rating (91.0) and 16th in yards per attempt (7.2). He was an MVP finalist.

This season, he is playing at a higher level - and getting the ball downfield. After five games, Lawrence is fourth in quarterback rating (106.3), eighth in completion percentage (67.1) and fifth in yards per attempt (8.2), along with 1,174 yards (14th) and 10 TDs (tied fifth).

Sam Darnold. Jared Goff. Baker Mayfield. There are plenty of examples of high quarterback draft picks who struggled for large parts of their careers before finding success in the right situation. The expectation is that everything will click immediately but that is simply not the reality for most QBs.

If you're the best in college, you're most likely joining the worst teams in the professional game, and it can take years for the stars to align.

Through the early period of Lawrence's NFL career, it would be no surprise for NFL RedZone's coverage to turn to Jacksonville and show a quarterback running for his life. You would see him scrambling around to avoid pressure, throwing from awkward positions... playing 'hero ball', essentially.

Now, watch Lawrence and you'll see cool, calm, composed and importantly, assured. He knows where his feet should be, where his eyes should look and where his team-mates will be at any given time. Coen has been crucial in helping Lawrence find a rhythm.

Look no further than Lawrence's stunning fourth-down throw to Parker Washington against the Eagles on Sunday. Feet, eyes, timing... touchdown.

Lawrence was slicing and dicing, dinking and dunking his way to 331 yards against Philadelphia, and it's becoming a common occurrence.

Lawrence has not been blessed with an 'alpha' receiver so far in his career. No disrespect to Marvin Jones, Christian Kirk or Calvin Ridley, but these aren't names you'd want to provide an elite quarterback. Brian Thomas Jr had an instant impact as a rookie in 2024 but has since dropped off, giving way to last season's top option: Washington.

In the 24-year-old, the Jaguars have found a gem. Sixth-round picks don't usually make too much of an impact, let alone develop into a team's top target by their fourth year.

Washington's one-handed grab in London showed the trust Lawrence has in him. According to ESPN , since Week 11 of last season, Washington has 17 catches for a league-best 381 yards on third and fourth downs. He was Lawrence's top target by a clear distance in that lone playoff game last year.

Lawrence is tremendous at spreading the ball around to multiple receivers but Washington tops the team with 22 catches, 352 yards and four TDs so far this campaign after doing the same last year (58-847-5). Don't be surprised to see more games like last Sunday (6-124-2).

It would be an oversight not to mention Jacksonville's improved defense at this point. Since Coen took over and brought defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile with him, the Jaguars have only allowed 18.5 points per game, behind only Seattle and Minnesota. This year, that number is 14.0 with only the Vikings (12.8) performing better.

They will be crucial for the Jags to make a deep run this season.

The Jaguars continue their London visit this Sunday, facing the desperation-mode Houston Texans at Wembley, live on Sky Sports . Houston started 0-4 but won last week and need a victory to keep their season alive.

The game is one of four divisional games for Jacksonville in their next six. If we are talking about a serious contender, this is a chance for Lawrence and company to show their credentials.

If you ask someone who their Super Bowl favourite is this season, they are most likely to say the Buffalo Bills, San Francisco 49ers, Kansas City Chiefs or Seattle Seahawks. How long before the Jaguars are one of the first teams mentioned?

articles.title: Projecting NFL Fire Sales for the League's Worst Teams Ahead of the 2026 Trade Deadline
articles.summary: Not that long ago, trades were a relative rarity in the NFL. But the times they are a-changin', and more and more NFL clubs are willing to play Let's Make a Deal—including during the season.
articles.body:
Not that long ago, trades were a relative rarity in the NFL. But the times they are a-changin', and more and more NFL clubs are willing to play Let's Make a Deal— including during the season.

We saw a significant deal go down recently, with the Arizona Cardinals sending wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans for a package headlined by a second-round selection in next year's draft.

With the trade deadline looming on November 10, we are likely to see even more deals struck over the next few weeks.

Most teams likely to trade away players and accumulate draft picks are franchises that have struggled this year—teams racking up losses and already looking toward the future.

There is no shortage of teams that fit that description after five weeks of the season—and a long list of players could be on the move before the trade deadline.

There isn't a more disappointing team in the NFL right now than the Los Angeles Chargers. They were expected to contend for an AFC West title in 2026. Instead, the Bolts are winless and the offense has imploded.

However, while there could be big changes coming soon for the Bolts, ESPN's Adam Schefter was quick to shoot down the idea that the Chargers could well and truly blow things up and trade quarterback Justin Herbert.

"The person basically cut me off mid-sentence," Schefter said , "stopped me in my tracks, and said, 'Let me be very clear about this. We have never even discussed that idea. The sentence should we trade Justin Herbert has never once been uttered in our organization, nor will it be.'"

The Chargers may be unwilling to deal Herbert, but there are other potential assets that could be moved. Wide receiver Quentin Johnston has been inconsistent, but he's a talented young pass-catcher whose exercised fifth-year option keeps him under contract through 2027.

Edge-rusher Tuli Tuipulotu is in a contract year, but he's just 24 and coming off a 13-sack season. Safety Derwin James Jr. has long been considered one of the best in the league at his position. Edge-rusher Khalil Mack could garner a Day 3 pick as a temporary fix for teams looking to upgrade the pass rush.

The biggest obstacle may be whether Los Angeles views its current struggles as grounds to sell at the deadline. As ESPN's Jeremy Fowler noted , one NFL executive said, "'I think it's going to be really difficult for them to admit when and if they need to trade guys.'"

After the New Orleans Saints started the season with a close loss to the Lions and a win over the Baltimore Ravens, it appeared there may be something brewing in the Big Easy.

Three losses later, the Saints are sitting at 1-4 and team owner Gayle Benson isn't happy.

"That is not acceptable to me," she said, via NOLA.com's Rod Walker . "And it falls short of what our fans truly deserve. I hear the frustration directed towards our team and our organization. It is not lost on me. Our fans invest their time and their hearts in the Saints. They are right to expect more than we have delivered."

It certainly appears the Saints are headed toward a sixth straight season of missing the playoffs. The problem in New Orleans is that even if the team wanted to sell at the deadline, there aren't many assets the team would be willing to part with that could bring a return.

Veteran edge-rusher Cameron Jordan might be amenable to ending his career with a playoff run, but the 37-year-old won't net more than a late-round pick.

With rookie Jeremiah Wright on the roster, the team could move veteran guard Cesar Ruiz, who was the subject of trade speculation earlier in the offseason. Juwan Johnson could generate some interest, too—he is fifth among tight ends in receptions and seventh in receiving yards.

A fire sale remains unlikely given general manager Mickey Loomis' reluctance to undertake a full rebuild, but it's still possible.

Given the Houston Texans just dealt a second-rounder to the Arizona Cardinals for wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr., the team doesn't appear to be willing to throw in the towel on the 2026 season—yet.

That could change as early as next week if they lose in London, but for now no fire sale is looming.

However, as bad as things are going in Houston, they are that much worse for the winless Titans, who look completely lost on offense.

Carter Bahns of CBS Sports expects Tennessee to already be looking forward to 2027 and potentially selling off veteran assets at the trade deadline:

"If a Titans breakthrough comes during the Robert Saleh era, it does not appear it will happen in Year 1. This franchise is still stuck in rebuild mode and needs to acquire as much draft capital as possible to round out its core of Cam Ward and Carnell Tate with more young prospects. That means cutting bait on what already looks like a lost season, parting with the tradeable veterans, hoping that Ward shows signs of improvement in the second half of the year and making good use of what should be another early first-round pick in 2027."

Defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons is the Titans' most valuable trade chip, but the team could be reluctant to part with their best defensive player. Edge-rusher Jermaine Johnson, who is slated to hit free agency next spring, is another matter.

On offense, veteran wide receiver Calvin Ridley has struggled to make an impact in Tennessee, but he was a 1,000-yard receiver as recently as two years ago. Tony Pollard is a capable veteran back who could appeal to a team with injury issues in the backfield.

If those veterans are unlikely to remain through the rebuild, Tennessee could consider moving them now to add draft capital.

Much like the Los Angeles Chargers, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers entered the 2026 season with postseason aspirations. Those hopes remain alive in a weak NFC South, but Tampa Bay didn't record its first win until last week, and a playoff berth appears unlikely.

If history is any indication, a fire sale isn't likely either. Buccaneers general manager Jason Licht has been on the job for well over a decade in Tampa, and you can count the number of in-season deals he has made (buying or selling) with one hand and still have fingers left over.

If the Buccaneers remain well below .500 when the deadline arrives, Licht may decide to buck historical precedent and try to jump-start a rebound year in 2027.

If so, there are assets for the GM to work with on both sides of the ball.

On defense, tackle A'Shawn Robinson, edge-rusher Yaya Diaby and cornerback Zyon McCollum could all generate interest. The first two are in contract years. The third is in the first year of an extension that pays him a relatively reasonable $16 million a season.

On offense, veteran wideout Chris Godwin isn't the player he once was, but the 30-year-old posted three straight 1,000-yard seasons from 2021 to 2023 and could be enticing for a playoff contender thin at wide receiver.

McCollum may be the only player on that list who remains on Tampa Bay's roster in 2027. If the Buccaneers don't view those veterans as part of their long-term plans, trading them now could provide additional draft capital.

There were no postseason aspirations in Miami this year. In fact, if the team dumps veteran talent at the trade deadline, it will mark the second fire sale of 2026—the Dolphins already purged vets like wide receiver Jaylen Waddle and edge-rusher Bradley Chubb in the spring.

Expectations were low for Miami, but its winless start has been particularly discouraging. There's a non-zero chance the Dolphins won't win a game this season.

Despite that, first-year head coach Jeff Hafley told reporters what he wants to see from his team.

"I want to see more consistency. I want to see better execution," he said. "I want to see the same fight. I want to see the same energy. I want to see the same connection."

Miami remains in the early stages of a substantial rebuild, so adding draft picks would be a sensible move, particularly by trading players on expiring contracts who are unlikely to return.

That's the case with both offensive tackle Austin Jackson and edge-rusher Josh Uche. Jackson has struggled this year, but experienced players at his position will always be in demand, if only as a one-year rental.

Defensively, Jordyn Brooks' new contract makes him difficult to deal, but given the play of rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, it's at least worth considering. Defensive tackle Zach Sieler isn't owed any guaranteed money after 2026, so the ninth-year veteran may be the most valuable trade commodity the Dolphins have.

Miami appears to be facing a multiyear rebuild, which could make veterans outside its long-term plans logical trade candidates.

The Arizona Cardinals were in some ways the genesis of this column, with their trade of wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans. But that doesn't mean the Redbirds are done selling.

Per Daniel Popper of The Athletic , there are multiple veterans on defense who could be sent packing in the next few weeks:

"The Cardinals already sold by trading away Harrison, and they could sell again before the deadline. Arizona has lost four straight games after beating the Chargers in the opener. On Sunday, they gave up 45 points to the Detroit Lions. Coach Mike LaFleur is in his first season. The Cardinals have some building to do with their roster. They should be in the market for future picks. Edge-rusher Baron Browning is on an expiring deal."

Sweat signed a four-year deal with the Cardinals in free agency in 2025. According to Popper, trading him would carry a substantial dead-money charge in 2027.

Browning and Sweat aren't the only veterans who could be available, especially on defense. Teams could have interest in former first-round pick Zaven Collins.

There would definitely be interest from playoff contenders in veteran safety Budda Baker, who has been named to the Pro Bowl after each of the last seven seasons.

At this stage of his career, a trade could give the 30-year-old an opportunity to join a contender after spending his entire 10-year career in Arizona.

The Cardinals' current struggles and roster needs could make acquiring future picks a priority.

articles.title: Updated Fantasy Football Week 6 Trade Value for Top 50 NFL Players
articles.summary: How are we doing, fantasy football players of the world?
articles.body:
How are we doing, fantasy football players of the world?

We all know fantasy can be a cruel mistress. Some weeks you score the second most points in the entire league, but your opponent is No. 1. Sometimes you find your roster ravaged by injuries or engulfed in confusing running-back committees. Maybe you chose to trust in Kyle Pitts Sr. as your tight end and it took five whole weeks for that to pay off.

Whatever your plight may be, the fantasy trade value chart is here to help in your efforts to patch up that sinking ship.

Players who would be ranked in the 51-100 range have a descending trade value between six and two. Players below the top-100 range have a value of one. Trade values are based on PPR scoring, so adjust according to your league's particular scoring settings. May the fantasy points be with you!

Only six players in fantasy football this season—Jahmyr Gibbs (30.7 FPG), Josh Allen (28.6), Jaxon Smith-Njigba (27.9), Kenneth Walker III (27.5), Puka Nacua (25.9) and Bijan Robinson (24.2)—are averaging more points per game played than Bowers (23.7).

And he's doing it at tight end, which gives him enormous positional value. He's averaging 5.5 more points per game than the No. 2 tight end in points-per-game-played, Trey McBride. That's a bigger gap than any other position (though Allen is close at 5.3 more points per week than Brock Purdy).

Stretch it out further, and Bowers is scoring 13.4 points more points per week than the No. 13 player at the position, Harold Fannin Jr., which is extraordinary value in 12-team leagues. Compare that to Allen, who is scoring 10.8 points more per week than the No. 13 QB (C.J. Stroud).

And while injuries are always a concern, maintaining this level of production is realistic. In 32 career games, Bowers is averaging 6.25 catches, 68.3 yards and 0.46 touchdowns, which translates to 15.8 fantasy points a game. That's obviously a drop from this season's gaudy output, but Bowers also has an upgrade at both quarterback (Kirk Cousins) and in offensive scheme with Klint Kubiak as head coach this season.

In other words, you shouldn't be shocked if his current three-game tear is in fact sustainable for the rest of the season. In his three healthy games this season, he's been targeted more times (34) than any other player on the Las Vegas Raiders.

So while there's really no good reason to trade him, you better be getting an elite, elite return if you do. And if you're the buyer, expect to pay a premium.

articles.title: Biggest Sleepers at Every Position for Week 6 Fantasy Football 2026
articles.summary: Fantasy football managers must work around bye weeks for Jahmyr Gibbs, Jared Goff, Sam LaPorta, Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, Chase Brown and Justin Jefferson in Week 6. That's not ideal if you're battling to stay alive in a guillotine league or trying to overcome a slow start.
articles.body:
Fantasy football managers must work around bye weeks for Jahmyr Gibbs, Jared Goff, Sam LaPorta, Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, Chase Brown and Justin Jefferson in Week 6. That's not ideal if you're battling to stay alive in a guillotine league or trying to overcome a slow start.

Fortunately, this week's sleeper list features a high-floor veteran quarterback, a potential RB1, an explosive wide receiver in a plus matchup, and a proven tight end on a scoring streak.

Four of the eight sleeper selections are on two teams, including a QB-WR stack that posted high-end numbers in Week 2.

Take a look at the biggest (and best) sleeper options at every position. They're all available in more than 50 percent of leagues, according to FantasyPros .

QB Kirk Cousins vs. Buffalo Bills (47 Percent Rostered)

Although the Las Vegas Raiders pulled Kirk Cousins for rookie Fernando Mendoza in the fourth quarter of their blowout loss to the New England Patriots, head coach Klint Kubiak reaffirmed that the veteran is still the starter.

So, Cousins is safe to start as a streamer option if Joe Burrow or Jared Goff is on your bench for a bye week.

Cousins threw three touchdown passes in each of his first three games of the season. His production dipped against the playoff-caliber Kansas City Chiefs and New England Patriots, but the Buffalo Bills don't have a champion-level defense like the Raiders' previous two opponents.

The Bills have allowed the fourth-most fantasy points to quarterbacks. Except for Justin Herbert, who's having an abysmal year under new Los Angeles Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, Buffalo has allowed at least 269 passing yards and multiple touchdowns to opposing quarterbacks. Cousins has done that in three games.

Furthermore, the Bills just played nearly 70 minutes of football in an overtime thriller against the Los Angeles Rams. Cousins can exploit a vulnerable secondary on tired legs.

RB Dameon Pierce vs. Carolina Panthers (8 Percent Rostered)

If you're in desperate need of a lead running back with Jahmyr Gibbs on a bye week, make sure you pick up Dameon Pierce.

According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , Saquon Barkley is week-to-week with a hamstring injury. He sat out Week 5 and missed practice on Wednesday.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that Eagles backup running back Will Shipley suffered a partial plantar fascia tear during the game against the Jacksonville Jaguars and could miss multiple weeks.

Against the Jaguars, Pierce led the Eagles backfield with 13 touches: 11 carries for 14 yards and two catches for minus-2 yards. It's not an ideal stat line, but Jacksonville gives up the fewest rushing yards and is a tough matchup for running backs.

If Barkley is out, Pierce gets a more favorable matchup against the Carolina Panthers, who give up the most yards per carry (5.4) and have allowed at least 132 rushing yards in three of their four games. In fantasy terms, Carolina allows the fifth-most points to running backs.

Pierce shouldn't be available in your league while Barkley's status remains uncertain.

RB Najee Harris vs. New Orleans Saints (8 Percent Rostered)

The New York Giants likely turned on Week 4 film to watch Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson Jr. run all over the New Orleans Saints defense, thinking they can emulate that approach with Cam Skattebo and Najee Harris.

The Saints have struggled mightily against the run, allowing 108-plus rushing yards in all their games, giving up the third-most rushing yards. By the way, they've allowed the most rushing scores (10) heading into Week 6.

Skattebo is the Giants' lead ball-carrier, but Harris has a role, logging at least five carries in three consecutive contests. Although that's not a large share of the rushing workload, he could see more touches after Skattebo fumbled for the fourth time this season in last week's game.

With the Saints allowing the most fantasy points to running backs, Harris, even as the Giants' No. 2 running back, is worth considering as a flex option.

WR Tre Tucker vs. Buffalo Bills (39 Percent Rostered)

Tre Tucker completes the Las Vegas Raiders sleeper stack. He's essentially the Raiders' No. 2 wide receiver because tight end Brock Bowers frequently lines up out wide in head coach Klint Kubiak's offense.

Tucker has been a low-end WR3/flex option for most of the season. After catching five passes for 119 yards and a touchdown against the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 2, he caught four passes in each of his next three games, recording between 41 and 44 receiving yards per outing.

This week, Tucker can rise above that flex floor and into WR2 territory in a plus matchup against the Buffalo Bills' 31st-ranked pass defense.

Tucker had his best game while Bowers sat out after knee surgery, but he has boom potential against a pass defense that has surrendered three touchdowns in back-to-back games. Buffalo is giving up the most fantasy points to wide receivers, so this could be a high-scoring game in which Tucker makes a few big plays.

WR Germie Bernard at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (17 Percent Rostered)

The Pittsburgh Steelers placed Michael Pittman Jr. on injured reserve with a foot injury. According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , fellow wideout Roman Wilson could miss a couple of weeks with a finger injury.

With two of its top three receivers down, Pittsburgh will likely expand rookie second-rounder Germie Bernard's role. He should see more snaps following his Week 5 performance against the Indianapolis Colts.

Last week, Bernard led the Steelers with nine targets, catching six passes for 80 yards. With DK Metcalf's inconsistent production, the first-year wideout could emerge in a solid role while Pittman and Wilson are out.

Bernard isn't in a smash spot for wideouts, but receiver-needy managers shouldn't shy away from his matchup. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers rank 20th in passing yards allowed.

In the Buccaneers' previous outing against the Dallas Cowboys, they gave up 130 yards and two touchdowns to George Pickens and 90 yards to Ryan Flournoy, who replaced an injured CeeDee Lamb.

WR Brandin Cooks vs. Washington Commanders (1 Percent Rostered)

The San Francisco 49ers desperately need healthy bodies at wide receiver after Deebo Samuel Sr. suffered a hamstring injury last Sunday.

According to The Athletic's Matt Barrows , Brandin Cooks is the next man up to fill a void in the 49ers' injury-riddled wide receiver corps.

In the 49ers' win over the Seattle Seahawks, Cooks recorded a seven-yard touchdown reception early in the fourth quarter, his only catch of the game. In an expanded role, he could see decent volume against one of the league's worst pass defenses.

The Washington Commanders have allowed the fourth-most passing yards and the third-most passing touchdowns. They're also giving up the fifth-most fantasy points to wide receivers.

Cooks is past his prime, but he has an intriguing matchup that puts him on the sleeper radar for managers who want a player in their lineup Monday night.

TE Pat Freiermuth at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (27 Percent Rostered)

If you don't quite trust a rookie like Germie Bernard to fill a void in the Pittsburgh Steelers' banged-up pass-catching group, consider Pat Freiermuth as an alternative. The sixth-year pro is a known commodity with a track record of solid production.

Although Freiermuth's receiving yards total has been modest, he's found the end zone recently, scoring three touchdowns over his last two outings. With the Steelers' wide receiver injuries, the sure-handed tight end may see more targets, which could boost his yardage.

Moreover, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers defense allows the 11th-most fantasy points per game to tight ends. It has surrendered touchdowns to Mike Gesicki, Blake Whiteheart and Tucker Kraft.

In a more prominent pass-catching role, Freiermuth could extend his scoring streak to three games and, for the first time this season, rack up 50-plus receiving yards.

TE Charlie Kolar at Kansas City Chiefs (1 Percent Rostered)

The Los Angeles Chargers offense is in complete disarray, and their receivers are banged up.

Quentin Johnston didn't play in the team's previous outing because of a chest injury. Ladd McConkey was active, but he didn't log any snaps while nursing a foot injury. Tre' Harris suited up but left early with a hamstring injury.

With multiple Chargers receivers injured, Charlie Kolar could see more targets in the passing game, just in time for a favorable matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs.

In Week 5, Kolar returned from a broken forearm and caught three passes for a team-leading 37 receiving yards. He didn't light up the box score, but his more prominent role in the passing game compared with Oronde Gadsden, who had a strong 2025 rookie campaign, is notable.

As the Chargers' top tight end, Kolar is a reasonable dart throw given that the Chiefs allow the third-most fantasy points to players at his position.

Even if you exclude Las Vegas Raiders All-Pro Brock Bowers, who also plays a wide receiver role, Kansas City allowed eight catches for 82 yards to Michael Mayer, five receptions and 55 yards to Greg Dulcich, six catches for 21 yards and a touchdown to Tyler Warren and four receptions for 43 yards and a score to Evan Engram.

Kolar is a deep sleeper who could fill a void if you're without Sam LaPorta this week.

Fantasy points scored against statistics are provided by FantasyPros .

Maurice Moton covers the NFL for Bleacher Report. You can follow him on Twitter @MoeMoton .

articles.title: Bleacher Report's Expert Week 6 2026 NFL Picks
articles.summary: After a cinematic Monday Night Football game between the Los Angeles Rams and Buffalo Bills, Bleacher Report's expert crew feels refreshed, especially since most of the panel nailed the pick.
articles.body:
After a cinematic Monday Night Football game between the Los Angeles Rams and Buffalo Bills, Bleacher Report's expert crew feels refreshed, especially since most of the panel nailed the pick.

Analysts Gary Davenport , Brad Gagnon , Kris Knox , Moe Moton , and Brent Sobleski , along with editors Wes O'Donnell and Ian Hanford , are at their best when howling at the moon. They're 10-6 on lone-wolf picks, which is a sign that when most of the panel zigs, maybe you should zag, which worked out for Knox, Gagnon and O'Donnell last week.

That said, our Week 6 breakdowns start out with a lone-wolf pick in favor of the home 'dog.

Moton's lead in the standings has dwindled to two wins; almost everyone is packed together with similar records going into Week 6. Let's get to the 14-game slate breakdown against the spread.

Lines are from FanDuel as of Wednesday, Oct. 14, at 4 p.m. ET. Check FanDuel for the latest odds info. Information on public betting trends is courtesy of the Action Network . ATS records are provided by Team Rankings .

Seattle Seahawks (3-2) at Denver Broncos (3-2)

In theory, an angry Seahawks team should have no issue moving the ball against a beat-up Denver defense, and the Broncos' offense doesn't appear to have the juice to keep pace in a shootout with Seattle. But this game isn't being played in theory. It's being played in Colorado.

We have already seen Denver beat two contenders in the Rams and Jaguars at Mile High. We have also seen the Seahawks hurt themselves with costly mistakes on the road. Add in the short week favoring the home team, and Denver wins this one outright.

The 49ers served the Seahawks a reality check in their road win over the reigning Super Bowl champions. Seattle has played sloppy football between Weeks 3 and 5, losing twice in that span.

After the loss to the 49ers, Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald acknowledged the team's ball-security issues. Seattle has eight turnovers in its last three outings.

Expect the Seahawks to be dialed in for a short week against the slow-starting Broncos, who are tied with the Tennessee Titans for the league-worst first-half scoring average, 4.6 points, per Team Rankings .

Seattle takes an early lead and holds on by just over a field goal.

Seahawks: Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Houston Texans (1-4) vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (4-1)

The Jaguars have looked to be a far better team than the Texans through the first five weeks, and they'll have the benefit of playing in London for the second straight week. However, I have a hard time trusting Jacksonville after last week's miracle win against the short-handed Eagles.

Sloppy play and poor decision-making should have cost the Jags the game last Sunday. I think they'll once again struggle to pull away against a very familiar opponent.

Yes, the Texans are 1-4, but C.J. Stroud has been playing extremely well, and Houston's 11th-ranked defense may have found the spark it needed in last week's win over the Titans—after DeMeco Ryans took back play-calling. Jacksonville may escape with another London win, but I think it'll be extremely close.

A win over the lowly Tennessee Titans isn't enough to start believing in the Texans. Plus, the Jaguars, who are one of the NFL's best teams this season, hold a home-field advantage. C.J. Stroud still ranks among the top-four quarterbacks in times sacked. Jacksonville features a talented defensive front capable of making life miserable for Stroud while placing the Texans back into the losing column.

Jaguars: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, O'Donnell, Sobleski

New York Jets (2-3) at New England Patriots (3-2)

The Pats have scored 74 points over their last two games, while the Jets have managed just 29. Scraping past Cleveland in an ugly home slog does little to validate New York, especially with New England picking up serious steam. The Patriots swept this series by a combined 45 points last season, and there's little reason to expect a different script here.

The spread is intriguing with this matchup, because the Jets fell by more than a touchdown only once during their three losses. Yes, quarterback Drake Maye is coming off his best game of the season and the Patriots are at home. However, the Jets own a top-four defense and the unit is particularly good against the pass--which should allow Aaron Glenn's crew to keep this game closer than the spread suggests.

Patriots: Davenport, Gagnon, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell

New Orleans Saints (1-4) at New York Giants (3-1-1)

Based on our 10-6 record on lone-wolf picks, it's not a good sign to see our panel all on the Giants, but it makes sense in this case.

The Saints field a one-dimensional, pass-heavy offense that lacks a counterpunch without a complementary run game. They've also turned the ball over at least three times in three of their five games and face a Giants squad that's tied for fifth in takeaways with eight.

Over five weeks, the Saints have allowed the most rushing touchdowns and the third-most rushing yards. Big Blue should steamroll New Orleans with Cam Skattebo and Najee Harris if they can hold onto the ball.

Ignore any Jameis Winston revenge game talk here. It means nothing. What does mean something is that the Giants experimented with a J.J. McCarthy package on offense in their tie with the Commanders last week. It was bad.

Winston responded well after the unsuccessful experiment, led Big Blue back from a 14-point fourth-quarter deficit, and put them in position to win.

Although the Giants neither won nor lost last week, now is not the time for them to get cute. And make no mistake: cute and unnecessary is exactly what a McCarthy package is and will be going forward. They do not need it.

New York leads the NFC East and faces a much tougher schedule in the coming weeks. This should be considered a must-win matchup for the home 'dogs. The Saints haven't played a road game in almost a month; their defense struggles to stop the run (third worst in the NFL), and they're tied for the league's worst turnover differential at minus-6.

The Giants need to pound the rock, open up the play-action game downfield for Jameis, and (hopefully) give their defense a chance to pin its ears back, defend with a lead, get after Tyler Shough, and force some turnovers.

This is a favorable matchup that the Giants should capitalize on.

Giants: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Tennessee Titans (0-5) at Indianapolis Colts (2-3)

This could be the week Tennessee's offense shows meaningful improvement.

The Titans face an Indianapolis defense that ranks in the bottom six against both the pass and the run. The Colts have only contained Houston, which was without wideout Nico Collins in Week 3, and Washington, which started rookie third-string quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis in London.

Before the Titans' matchup with the Texans last week, Cam Ward and Carnell Tate started to click in the passing game. Tate caught nine passes for 145 yards against the Baltimore Ravens, while Tennessee trailed for most of that game.

Still, the Titans' quarterback-receiver duo showed progress in their rapport that could carry over into this game against a porous pass defense. The Ward-Tate connection with a sprinkle of Wan'Dale Robinson puts Indianapolis on upset alert.

Aside from a lopsided Week 1 loss to the Baltimore Ravens, the Colts have been competitive every week. At 2-3, Shane Steichen's squad needs to make a serious push or risk yet another playoff-less campaign. The Titans arrive at the right time. A home game against an inferior opponent should be exactly what Indianapolis needs before three difficult matchups against the Minnesota Vikings, Jacksonville Jaguars and Dallas Cowboys.

Colts: Davenport, Gagnon, Knox, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Chicago Bears (2-3) at Atlanta Falcons (2-3)

I'm backing the Bears after a terrible showing against Green Bay last week. Caleb Williams may or may not return, but this team will be fired up knowing their QB will be back soon regardless. Michael Penix Jr.'s injury is a large part of why Atlanta lost in Week 5, and he may return for this one, but I like the Bears to surprise some in a bit of a shootout here.

On paper, this feels like a mismatch in Chicago's favor. Atlanta's defense is dealing with multiple key injuries, and the status of Michael Penix Jr. (ribs) is still unclear. Meanwhile, the Bears expect Caleb Williams to return from a hamstring injury.

However, I get the strange feeling that Williams could be shaky in his first game back. That could be a massive problem if Kyle Monangai (toe) can't go, and the Bears cannot consistently run the ball effectively.

I also have serious concerns about a Chicago defense that has only looked good on occasion this season. The Bears rank 22nd in yards per carry allowed, and that's not a rate I like against Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson Jr. on the road.

Falcons: Davenport, Gagnon, Knox, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Baltimore Ravens (4-1) at Cleveland Browns (3-2)

The Browns are 2-0 at home and haven't dropped a game in Cleveland by more than a field goal in their last five outings. They held a fourth-quarter lead over Baltimore at this site last November, and now they catch a banged-up Lamar Jackson—if he suits up at all. Count on Cleveland keeping this within one score against a flawed Ravens team that has merely been surviving.

The Ravens are optimistic that Lamar Jackson will play Sunday, which will provide a significant advantage over the Browns, even if Baltimore's quarterback isn't as mobile as he normally is.

Meanwhile, Deshaun Watson had done enough to quiet critics after Cleveland began the season with a 3-1 record, before last week's loss to the New York Jets. However, he has not performed at a high level. The Browns' QB1 has simply been good enough not to get in the way of the team, which is exactly why Baltimore should be considered the favorite in this contest and capable of clearing the spread.

Browns: Gagnon, Hanford, Moton, O'Donnell

Pittsburgh Steelers (3-2) at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (1-4)

It's possible Tampa Bay found a recipe for success running the ball last week, but the Steelers did just do a good job of containing Jonathan Taylor in their Week 5 win. The Steelers offense has found a rhythm lately with the quick passing game and a heavy dose of playmaking from Jaylen Warren. It's never pretty in Pittsburgh, but this feels like another win for Mike McCarthy to push his team further up the AFC hierarchy.

The Steelers looked like legitimate contenders last week against the Colts, and they should be able to rattle a Buccaneers team starting an undrafted rookie at quarterback. However, Jalon Daniels looked like a signal-caller who isn't easily flustered during last Thursday's win in Dallas.

The Bucs have had extra time to prepare for this one, and they have a defense that is allowing just 3.3 yards per carry. They can make Pittsburgh one-dimensional offensively, and given the Steelers' injuries at receiver, that's a major concern.

I'd still consider backing Pittsburgh here if the Steelers hadn't looked like a lesser team on the road in 2026. They have, though, and I think there's a very real chance they'll fall to 0-3 away from Acrisure Stadium this week.

Steelers: Davenport, Hanford, Moton, Sobleski

Carolina Panthers (2-2) at Philadelphia Eagles (2-3)

The Eagles are desperate after a heartbreaking loss to the Jaguars in London last week, and I think they'll right the ship a bit here against the Panthers coming off their bye week.

Philadelphia has been decimated by injuries, but it sounds like DeVonta Smith and Saquon Barkley could return in Week 6.

The offensive line has had its share of issues, but I think a veteran Eagles team shows enough pluck to keep their heads above water for at least one more week.

I'm done trying to figure out the Eagles. The Eagles clearly cannot figure out the Eagles. And while the Panthers' defense is a great opportunity for any offense to get right, Carolina had a bye week and then some to prepare for Philly. This Panthers team has defied the odds and shown up in tough situations since last season.

It would be easy to say, "This is the week the Eagles figure it out," injuries aside. But with Nick Sirianni's team, I'll believe it when I see it.

Give me these points in a virtual pick'em, since I'm taking Bryce Young's Panthers to win outright.

Panthers: Davenport, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Arizona Cardinals (1-4) at Los Angeles Rams (2-3)

This feels like a game in which a late touchdown allows the underdog to cover.

The Cardinals have already covered one large road spread this season, and a late touchdown could help them cover another against the Rams.

This is too big a number to feel truly comfortable with. On its face, the game has backdoor cover written all over it. But the Cardinals are really stacking some bad losses with Jacoby Brissett under center despite his being serviceable enough to generate statistics in most games.

The Rams are coming off yet another brutal loss. If ever there was a time to blow the doors off an opponent, this is it. Matthew Stafford's last two games against the Cardinals: seven touchdown passes, zero interceptions, and a 22.5-point average margin of victory. The 2-3 Rams haven't really found themselves yet this year. It's time for both sides of the ball to show up, and with that comes a two-touchdown-plus cover.

Rams: Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Los Angeles Chargers (0-5) at Kansas City Chiefs (4-0)

I hate taking this many points in a divisional game, but the Chargers just look broken. Justin Herbert is making puzzling decisions, and you're starting to hear rumors of a potential sell-off at November's trade deadline.

Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes are historically dominant coming off a bye week, and I don't see that changing here as the Chargers lose by double digits and inexplicably fall to 0-6.

The Chargers usually play the Chiefs tough. In fact, in Justin Herbert's career—11 games against Kansas City—he's 4-7, with the game decided by an average of 6.3 points per game, and the last five meetings were all one-score games. As much as I want to see this as an opportunity for Herbert to turn around the incredibly negative narrative surrounding his 0-5 start this season, I just cannot do it.

Andy Reid-coached teams are 22-5 straight up coming out of the bye week. The Chiefs have rediscovered some of the swagger we have come to expect from a Patrick Mahomes team.

I can see this game being more competitive than the final score suggests. Picture the Chargers reaching Kansas City's red zone down nine or 10 points with three to four minutes remaining, committing a costly turnover and never getting the ball back.

I'll lay the points with the Chiefs because that's how these teams are playing right now.

Chiefs: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Buffalo Bills (4-1) at Las Vegas Raiders (3-2)

Admittedly, there is some letdown potential here, especially given Buffalo's shaky defense and a week spent on the West Coast. But it will likely take multiple Bills turnovers and an unusually sloppy performance to keep this game close.

This stretch was supposed to reveal who the Raiders really are. Two weeks in, they look improved from 2025, but they have yet to show they're a good team.

Despite concerns about its receiving corps, Buffalo's potent offense should prevent the Raiders from pulling off an upset.

The Raiders no-showed on their East Coast trip last week, but that may be a blip rather than the start of a trend. Aside from the previous outing, the Raiders have scored at least 26 points.

Going back home, Las Vegas faces Buffalo's 28th-ranked scoring defense, which allows the third-most yards. Also, the Bills are coming off a hard-fought Monday night contest that went deep into overtime. Don't be surprised if they come out flat.

The Raiders should look much better at home against a poor defense to keep this game within a touchdown.

Bills: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Dallas Cowboys (2-3) at Green Bay Packers (3-2)

This isn't an easy call. The Packers just routed the Chicago Bears, Dallas is on the road, and the Cowboys defense continues to struggle—again.

Until last week, though, the Packers defense didn't exactly look like the 1962 squad. They can't generate pressure consistently ( 29th in team pass rush win rate ) or stop the run (127.6 yards per game allowed).

In a battle of bad defenses, give me the better offense. That's Dallas.

The Packers woke up in a big way against Chicago, and they should carry that momentum into Sunday night against an untrustworthy Dallas squad.

The Cowboys lack bite defensively and staying power on offense. Dallas might hang around, but I'm comfortable laying less than a field goal with Green Bay at Lambeau.

Cowboys: Davenport, Knox, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Washington Commanders (1-3-1) at San Francisco 49ers (5-0)

That Week 5 late-game collapse could carry over, especially with Washington already struggling under Dan Quinn.

The Commanders' secondary looks poorly equipped to contain Brock Purdy, Mike Evans and San Francisco's offense, making this a difficult cross-country matchup for Jayden Daniels.

Coming off of arguably the biggest overtime blunder in recent memory, the Commanders should probably be even bigger underdogs in this one. Washington appears to be on the verge of imploding, while the 49ers have looked and played like the best team in football through five weeks.

While most logic—along with the rest of our panel—says to back the 49ers as home favorites, I think we could see the sort of strange outcome that has been all too common through the early season.

Injuries continue to mount for San Francisco, and I think losing Deebo Samuel Sr. will have a bigger impact on the 49ers' offense than most realize. I also don't think this is quite the mismatch that records and recent results might suggest.

I do believe San Francisco will get to 6-0. However, I think the emotional hangover of stealing a win in Seattle last week, coupled with a solid Commanders run defense, can make this one closer than expected.

49ers: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

articles.title: A Harbaugh in trouble, problems in the City of Angels and a London showdown: What to watch in Week 6 of the NFL
articles.summary: Five weeks into the NFL season, three teams remain unbeaten, a Super Bowl favorite is suddenly struggling and one high-profile head coach is already feeling the heat.
articles.body: Five weeks into the NFL season, three teams remain unbeaten, a Super Bowl favorite is suddenly struggling and one high-profile head coach is already feeling the heat. With division rivalries, a Sunday night shootout and a crucial London showdown on tap, Week 6 could tell us a lot about which teams are legitimate contenders and which are headed for disappointment. Here’s what to know ahead of this week’s NFL action. The Undefeateds We’re down to just three undefeated teams, and none has been more impressive than the San Francisco 49ers. Kyle Shanahan has his team off to a 5-0 start for the third time in seven years, and the wins couldn’t be much more impressive. The 49ers have already beaten three of last season’s conference finalists: the Denver Broncos, Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams. They’re the first team since the 1981 Broncos to notch three wins over the previous season’s conference finalists in their first five games. If the MVP award were handed out today, it would be going to Brock Purdy. The former Mr. Irrelevant was fabulous once again in San Francisco’s 32-29 win over division rival Seattle. Purdy leads the NFL with 13 touchdown passes and has thrown just two interceptions. And 6-0 appears to be on the horizon. The reeling Washington Commanders (after last week’s brutal tie to the New York Giants) come to town for Monday Night Football, where Shanahan has been nearly unbeatable at 7-1. Meanwhile, the Minnesota Vikings sail into their bye week with a perfect 5-0 record. Their flawless start has been one of the season’s biggest surprises. The Kansas City Chiefs return from their bye week well-rested and sitting at 4-0. Waiting for them are the lowly, winless Chargers, who are having an absolute nightmare of a season (we’ll get to them later on…). And if things weren’t already bad enough for Los Angeles, facing Andy Reid coming off a bye is about the last thing any team wants. Reid is an incredible 22-5 in games following a bye week. Harbaugh on the hot seat Week 6 is right around the time when NFL coaches start feeling their seats getting a little warmer. But right now, nobody’s seat is hotter than the one under Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh. Many expected LA to be a playoff team this season, but through five games, it’s looked like anything but. Once again, injuries have taken a toll on the offensive line, but that’s far from the only problem. Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel’s system doesn’t seem to be clicking, and a defense that was expected to be a strength hasn’t gotten going at all. Remember, Harbaugh was the blockbuster hire of January 2024, fresh off winning a national championship at Michigan. The Chargers handed him a reported five-year, $80 million contract with one goal in mind: Get this franchise to the Super Bowl. Well, that’s certainly not happening this year. At this point, the bigger question might be whether Harbaugh even makes it through the season. And with a trip to Kansas City up next, things could get even uglier before they get better. Another reason to panic in the City of Angels? Things aren’t exactly sunny over at the neighbor’s place, either. Rams head coach Sean McVay said he felt sick after Monday night’s stunning overtime loss to the Bills dropped his team to 2-3. It’s easy to understand why. The Rams became the first team in NFL history to lose a game despite piling up more than 400 total yards, recording at least 30 first downs, scoring five touchdowns, converting at least 50% of their third downs and committing zero turnovers. That’s almost impossible to do. Yet somehow, the Rams found a way. A blocked potential game-winning field goal proved costly, and the Rams have already moved on from kicker Harrison Mevis following his early-season struggles. So, is it time to panic in Los Angeles? Probably not. The Rams’ next four games are against the Arizona Cardinals, Las Vegas Raiders, Chargers and Commanders. They’ll likely be heavy favorites in all four, giving them a golden opportunity to turn things around in a hurry. And here’s the craziest part: Despite sitting at 2-3, the Rams are still the betting favorites to win the Super Bowl. Clearly, the oddsmakers aren’t ready to hit the panic button just yet. Sunday night shootout? The Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers renew their rivalry on Sunday Night Football, and if recent history tells us anything, we should probably expect plenty of points. The last two meetings between these teams have produced absolute fireworks. Last September, they played to a wild 40-40 tie. In the 2024 playoffs, Green Bay went into Dallas and embarrassed the Cowboys in a 48-32 rout. That’s 160 combined points in two games! Dallas has tried just about everything to fix its struggling defense. The latest move was trading for cornerback Joey Porter Jr., although he missed last week’s loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The good news for the Cowboys is they’ll have 10 days of rest heading into this matchup at Lambeau Field. The bad news? They’re running into a red-hot Jordan Love and a Packers offense that just put up 31 points against the Chicago Bears. If Dallas can’t find a way to slow down Love, this could turn into another long night for the Cowboys’ defense. One thing seems pretty safe to predict: The scoreboard operator at Lambeau could be busy. Texans’ season on the line in London For the third time since 2023, the Jacksonville Jaguars have made London their home away from home for two straight weeks. After beating the Eagles 19-17 at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, the Jags now head to famed Wembley Stadium looking for a London sweep against the Houston Texans. Jacksonville swept both of its London games in 2023 and split its two games across the pond in 2024. While another win would be nice for the 4-1 Jaguars, this game is an absolute must-win for the 1-4 Texans. Houston managed to keep its season alive last week with a victory over the lowly Tennessee Titans, but there’s still almost no margin for error if a postseason berth is on the cards. Remember, only one team in NFL history has started 0-4 and made the playoffs: the 1992 San Diego Chargers. The Texans avoided that fate by picking up their first win, but at 1-4, they’re still facing a massive uphill battle. And losing to an AFC South rival would only make things worse. The good news is that the schedule offers some hope. After Jacksonville, Houston’s next four games are against the Giants, Chargers, Cleveland Browns and Indianapolis Colts. That’s a stretch where the Texans could realistically put together a winning streak and climb right back into the playoff picture. But first, they have to take care of business in London. A win keeps hope alive. A loss could have Houston looking toward next season before Halloween. Full Week 6 schedule Thursday Seattle Seahawks @ Denver Broncos, 8:15 p.m. ET Sunday Houston Texans @ Jacksonville Jaguars (in London, UK), 9:30 a.m. ET New York Jets @ New England Patriots, 1 p.m. ET Carolina Panthers @ Philadelphia Eagles, 1 p.m. ET Pittsburgh Steelers @ Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 1 p.m. ET Baltimore Ravens @ Cleveland Browns, 1 p.m. ET Chicago Bears @ Atlanta Falcons, 1 p.m. ET New Orleans Saints @ New York Giants, 1 p.m. ET Tennessee Titans @ Indianapolis Colts, 1 p.m. ET Arizona Cardinals @ Los Angeles Rams, 4:05 p.m. ET Los Angeles Chargers @ Kansas City Chiefs, 4:25 p.m. ET Buffalo Bills @ Las Vegas Raiders, 4:25 p.m. ET Dallas Cowboys @ Green Bay Packers, 8:20 p.m. ET Monday Washington Commanders @ San Francisco 49ers, 8:15 p.m. ET

articles.title: Bradley Chubb's detailed version of Alaric Jackson punch incident paints Rams lineman as a hothead
articles.summary: Bradley Chubb gave a moment-by-moment account of the trash talk that led to Alaric Jackson's punch, which then led to a second NFL suspension.
articles.body: Alaric Jackson's fateful punch of Bradley Chubb, which has been in the news cycle for multiple days, finally received a firsthand explanation from the man on the receiving end of the blow. On the same day the NFL reduced Jackson's suspension from two games to one, Chubb gave reporters a moment-by-moment account of what happened. And, frankly, Chubb's account paints Jackson as overreacting, if the Buffalo Bills linebacker is to be believed. RAMS OFFENSIVE LINEMAN PUNCHES BILLS LINEBACKER AFTER THRILLING GAME: 'TEMPERS GOT FLARED' Chubb admitted that the highly charged fourth quarter between the Bills and Rams played on everyone's emotions. Chubb said both he and Jackson were "talking junk" to each other and admitted he carries some blame. "I'm not going to say to y'all I don't have any fault in the situation," Chubb admitted. "I'll tell you exactly what I said. I heard I've been talking about his mom and different things. That's not true at all." RAMS TACKLE ALARIC JACKSON WINS APPEAL, WILL MISS JUST ONE GAME FOR PUNCHING BILLS' BRADLEY CHUBB So what's Chubb's truth? "I went up to him, I said, 'Hey, we're gonna see y'all [butt] again,'" Chubb said, "and when we see y'all again, that chip ain't going to save you. That tight end, that guard is not going to save you. That's what I said." So, let's understand the footballspeak here: Chubb claims he warned Jackson that the next time they meet, presumably in the Super Bowl, the Rams tackle won't be helped by Los Angeles running backs chipping Chubb or tight ends and guards helping with double-teams. "And then he said, 'What you say?'" Chubb added. Jackson approached Chubb and got closer. "People said I put my hand in his face," Chubb continued, now backing away from the huddle of reporters to demonstrate how he started counting off things that wouldn't help block him next time. NFL SUSPENDS 49ERS LINEBACKER ONE GAME FOR SIDELINE SCUFFLE THAT INCLUDED HEADBUTT TO SEAHAWKS PLAYER "I said, 'The chip's not going to save you. The guard's not going to ... boom." Chubb said that after the punch he thought about how to respond but obviously decided not to punch back. "There's so many different ways you can react," he said. "Everybody wants you to react a certain way. Everybody wants you to do a certain thing, but it's like, boom. I got to think about where I'm at, what situation I'm in. "My team needs me. They brought me here to play and to be a leader. And I feel like if I would have reacted, if I would have did anything in both of those situations, I'm not doing what they brought me here to do." ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! Whether Chubb's account is 100% accurate or not there are things that are not refutable. Jackson swung, thus violating NFL policy. Chubb did not swing which is the reason he's not suspended for Sunday's game against the Las Vegas Raiders. And while Chubb moves forward, Jackson suffers another black mark on his record because this will be his second NFL suspension. Jackson was suspended in September 2024 for violating the NFL Personal Conduct Policy in connection to an encounter with a woman pertaining to the taping of their intimate relations. And in an unrelated incident on the morning of June 9, 2026, Jackson was arrested after Los Angeles police responded to a domestic disturbance call at his West Hills home late the previous night. Police booked him on suspicion of felony domestic violence and set bail at $50,000. Jackson was never formally charged because the Los Angeles City Attorney’s Office assigned the case to a pre-filing diversion program. Officials said the matter remained open and could be reconsidered if new developments emerged. It's unclear if assaulting an opposing player after a football game qualifies as new developments, but it certainly paints Jackson as a hothead. FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: Deshaun Watson on Sluggish Offense: "The Opportunity is Right There in Front of Us"
articles.summary: BEREA, Ohio -- After leading the Browns on three-straight fourth quarter drives to win the game, Deshaun Watson and the offense took a step back in the loss...
articles.body:
BEREA, Ohio -- After leading the Browns on three-straight fourth quarter drives to win the game, Deshaun Watson and the offense took a step back in the loss to the Jets. Watson did lead the Browns to a drive to take the lead in the fourth quarter, but after the Browns fell behind, could not rally them on three late attempts.

The Browns are averaging 18.6 points a game, tied for 27th in the NFL

Watson was asked what the offense can do to get going.

"It's a long season," Watson said before practice on Wednesday. "Some opportunities right in front of us. We can't dwell on what happened Sunday. We watch the tape on Monday, 24-hour rule, have an off day Tuesday, and then come in today and focus on the next opponent.

"The opportunity is right there in front of us, and we got to put in the work throughout the week, so we're prepared to have a chance to go for that opportunity on Sunday."

After five games, Watson's QB rating is still 94.1, which is eighth in the NFL. ESPN's Total QBR has him at 48.4, which is 21st in the NFL.

Through five games, Watson is 95-of-148 for 1,010 with a completion percentage of 64.2 percent. He has seven touchdowns and two interceptions. He has been sacked 19 times and has lost two fumbles

Watson continues to be effective running and is second on the team with 37 rushes for 167 yards (4.5 avg.), including a long of 21 yards, which is the second longest run for the Browns this season.

The Browns are 29th in the NFL in offense, averaging 273.6 yards a game. The Browns are 21st in rushing, averaging 94.2 yards a game, while rank 26th in the NFL in passing, averaging 179.4 yards a game.

The Ravens are 4-1, but their defense is allowing 325.6 yards a game (No. 14 in the NFL). They are 12th in rushing defense (102.0) and 18th in passing defense (223.6).

The Ravens have allowed 23-, 18-, 31-, 24- and 23-points a game for an average 23.8 points a game, 19th in the NFL.

Todd Monken said the Ravens defensive scheme is different under Jesse Minter and a new coaching staff, but the personnel he is familiar with, is similar.

"Oh, it's changed dramatically in terms of – I think the league has changed dramatically in terms of defensive coordinators' approaches to the way the game has changed in terms of analytics, and offenses taking four downs and their approach being more aggressive," Monken said. "But the personnel is very similar. They've added some pieces, but the personnel is still very similar."

Watson was sacked eight times last Sunday and he was asked what will it take to get that corrected.

"Just make sure we're all on the same page and we're communicating and we're on one line," he said. "We can operate a little bit faster and pick things up. We just all got on the same page. That's pretty much it."

The Browns have played five games together as an offense, but Watson said it was just a work in progress.

"Just more reps, more opportunities we get, communication throughout the week, watching film together, seeing what we're seeing, basically communicating what I'm seeing and what they're seeing, and just trying to be on the same page as much as possible," he said. "So again, we have five new guys, two of them rookies, three guys from different schemes. We just put them all in one, and we just try to communicate and try to be on the same page as much as possible."

The Browns have had an inconsistent rushing game all season, which has not helped the offense.

"It is definitely helpful, overall, not for the quarterback position, but for the whole team," Watson said. "Being able to run the ball is definitely one of the hardest things you have to do in this league, is to be able to run the ball. But when you can do that, it opens up a lot of other things for sure."

The Browns will be challenged in the running game if Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson are unable to play. Judkins injured his ankle against the Jets and has been in a walking boot, while Sampson was just designed to return to practice after missing the past four games with a knee injury. He did not practice on Wednesday. Raheim Sanders was placed on injured reserve on Tuesday with a hip injury and the Browns signed running back Audric Estime to the active roster from the Vikings' practice squad.

Estime and Jaleel McLaughlin are the only two running backs on the roster that were not on the injured list on Wednesday.

If Judkins and Sampson cannot play on Sunday, the Browns won't have a running back who was with the team in training camp.

"Well, it's part of the next man up. Right?" Monken said. "That's why you keep bringing in players and getting them up to speed, and we'll see, as the week goes on, who we'll have available."

The Browns also have running back Jaret Patterson on the practice squad.

Concepcion Back at practice: Only three days after being knocked out of the Jets game with a blow to the head by S Minkah Fitzpatrick. Concepcion regained consciousness and walked off the field and went to the locker room/ He was quickly ruled out for the game.

"Just from a player's health perspective, it's cool that it wasn't worse than it was, and so that's probably the biggest thing from a health standpoint," Monken said.

Concepcion remained in the concussion protocol Wednesday and was listed as limited. Concepcion, the No. 24 pick in April, has 18 catches for 149 yards, with no touchdowns.

Walking Wounded: Both teams combined for 36 players on the Wednesday injury report, despite both teams having played five games The Browns had 17 players listed, including five starters not practicing on Wednesday due to injury, including RB Quinshon Judkins (ankle), LB Carson Schwesinger (ankle) DE, DT Maliek Collins (foot), DT Mason Graham (knee, ankle), and OT Tytus Howard (knee).

Others not practicing were DT Mike Hall (ankle), DE Derek Barnett (ankle), G Teven Jenkins (back) and TE Carsen Ryan (calf).

Monken said he has not ruled any player out.

"We're not going to rule anybody in or out today, but we've got a number of guys dealing with some minor issues, and we'll see today and the rest of the week."

The Ravens had 19 listed on their injury report, including QB Lamar Jackson (ankle), who did not practice.

Designated for Return: In addition RB Dylan Sampson has been designated for return and is eligible to return to practice. Sampson was on the field for the first time on Wednesday, but he did not practice.

Monken was asked if Sampson could play on Sunday.

"I think there's a chance," he said. "He'll be out there today, and we're excited that his window has been opened."

RB Raheim Sanders was placed on injured reserve on Tuesday with a hip injury and will miss at least four games. RB Audric Estime was signed off of the Vikings' practice squad and practiced on Wednesday for the first time.

Orlovsky's assessment focused on Purdy's efficiency, decision-making and ability to distribute the football within San Francisco's offensive system. Since becoming the 49ers' starter, Purdy has demonstrated an ability to execute the scheme while taking advantage of the team's offensive talent. His performances have strengthened his reputation as a productive starter despite entering the league as the final selection of the 2022 NFL Draft.

Purdy's rise from irrelevancy to an established starting quarterback remains a notable development in the league. He took over after injuries affected San Francisco's quarterback depth during his rookie season and helped lead the team to the NFC Championship Game. The following season, he guided the 49ers to Super Bowl LVIII, further raising expectations surrounding his long-term role with the franchise.

His statistical efficiency has also contributed to the discussion about his place among NFL passers. Purdy has produced strong passing numbers while operating an offense built around timing, yards after the catch and opportunities downfield. His ability to identify defensive coverage and deliver accurate throws has helped San Francisco maintain a productive passing attack, although evaluations of his performance often consider the quality of his supporting cast.

Orlovsky shared his thoughts about how Purdy has been playing this season. This can be seen in a video shared by NFL on ESPN's official Instagram account.

The quarterback's standing among the league's elite remains a subject of debate, particularly when comparing individual production with team success. Supporters point to his accuracy and consistency, while broader assessments also examine how much his surroundings contribute to his results. Orlovsky's evaluation adds another perspective to that discussion as the 49ers continue to rely on Purdy to direct their offense.

San Francisco's ambitions will depend in part on maintaining consistent quarterback play throughout the season. Purdy's continued development and ability to perform against challenging defenses will help shape the team's prospects in a competitive NFC. Orlovsky's assessment reflects the growing attention surrounding the quarterback , whose journey from a late draft pick to a central figure in San Francisco has made him one of the league's closely watched players.

articles.title: Jets Re-Sign Linebacker Less Than 24 Hours After Cutting Him
articles.summary: The Jets cut LB Troy Reeder then brought him back the next day. This roster move shows how the team uses the practice squad to keep depth without losing a pl...
articles.body:
The New York Jets made a bold roster move that shocked no one who follows the league rules closely. On Wednesday, veteran linebacker Troy Reeder was added to the practice squad. This happened less than 24 hours after they announced they were cutting him. It is a clear example of roster gymnastics at the NFL level. The team needed to clear a spot, so they released him.

This move works because of how the league handles service time. Reeder is 32 years old and has enough years in the league to be a vested veteran. That status means he does not have to go through waivers when the team cuts him. The NFLPA explained the rule clearly.

"If you have earned three or more credited seasons since 1993, you are vested, meaning you are entitled to benefits negotiated under the CBA," the NFLPA posted, according to Heavy.com . This rule protects the player's benefits and lets the team keep him in the fold.

If Reeder had fewer years, another team could have claimed him off waivers. The Jets would have lost him for good. Instead, they used the system to their advantage. They can tell Reeder they will release him to make other moves, then bring him back once the dust settles. That appears to be exactly what happened here. It is a smart play that keeps a reliable special teams guy on the roster without using an active spot.

Reeder is not just a practice squad filler. He has real experience and has played in big games before. As part of the Los Angeles Rams, he secured a Super Bowl ring. He spent six of his first eight seasons there. The Jets need that kind of stability on their special teams unit.

Jets editorial contributor Amanda Vogt stated that Reeder rejoined the practice squad following his Tuesday release. She mentioned his initial practice squad signing occurred on Sept. 2, followed by an active roster move on Sept. 22. Playing in 85 special teams snaps, he recorded 4 tackles across four games where he dressed.

The team values his presence even if they do not have a spot for him on the active roster right now. Keeping him close means he knows the playbook and the coaching staff. It saves them from having to teach a new guy the system. This is a low-risk way to keep depth for a team that is trying to find its footing this season.

The Jets are also looking good on defense after their win over the Browns. They secured a 17-12 victory on Sunday at MetLife Stadium. The weather was terrible, but the team still got it done. In the NFL Media Group's recent power rankings, Nick Shook ranked the Jets at No. 20.

He wrote, "It was an admittedly ugly game for both sides, but the Jets finally finished on the victorious side. The inclement weather may distort the overall evaluation of Sunday's contest, but what's undeniable was the effectiveness of New York's aggressive pass rush, which piled up eight sacks and shut down Cleveland's offense (save for one late touchdown drive)."

Six different players recorded a sack in that win. The defense is stepping up when it matters most. With Reeder back on the squad and the pass rush clicking, the team has a chance to build momentum before their next game on Sunday. They face the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium.
